mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% YoY signals robust economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, the economy is in a restrictive monetary policy regime, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 YoY < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) signals increased consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth is negative for two consecutive months and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 1.5%, the economy is in a supply-side contraction with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO negative growth for 2 months and FEDFUNDS > 1.5%
regime_hint: supply-side contraction with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO has negative growth for 2 months and FEDFUNDS > 1.5%.
